array_contraction.collision_rule: A[t,i] and A[t+2,i] share a physical region but are not simultaneously live

logical_values.boundary_projection: if t == T then public A[T,i] is exported from A2[T mod 2,i]
if t == T then public A[T,i] is exported from Buf[T mod 2,i]
consumer_events: S_step_buffered(t+1,i) reads Buf[cur(t+1),i] when t < T

phase_projection.init: Buf[0][i] represents A[0][i] before the first step

double_buffering.read_write_role_obligation: each step reads cur(t) and writes next(t), never the reverse
double_buffering.swap_obligation: after each step, next(t) becomes cur(t+1) and cur(t) becomes reusable

inter_array_reuse.collision_rule: T1[i] and T2[i] share Buf[i] only across disjoint phase intervals

logical_values.boundary_projection: public C[i] is committed before Buf[i] is reused
public D[i] is committed after reading Buf[i]

inter_array_reuse.storage_compatibility: T1[i], T2[i], and Buf[i] have identical element layout and extent

caveat: The .scop skeleton shows folded physical storage; lifetime and phase correctness is in this JSON witness.
required_obligations: physical reuse is allowed only when logical valid intervals are disjoint
every read is linked to a producer whose value is still valid
each kill or reuse event is after the old logical value's last consumer
final public outputs are projected or copied before reused private storage is hidden
all physical regions have compatible element layout, extent, and bounds
phase projections such as modulo or cur/next are supplied by the witness sidecar, not by raw OpenScop access rows
